title: In 1964 the Ground Shook for Four Minutes and Raised a 220-Foot Wave

scenes.text: In 1964, the ground in Alaska shook for four minutes.
It was a magnitude nine point two, the second biggest quake ever recorded.
Only the 1960 Chile earthquake was bigger.
Parts of the coast dropped eight feet.
Landslides and the quake sent waves racing across the fjords.
One wave climbed about two hundred and twenty feet at Valdez.
That's taller than a twenty-story building.

description:
In 1964 the ground in Alaska shook for four minutes.
It was a magnitude 9.2 earthquake, the second biggest ever recorded, and one wave climbed about 220 feet at Valdez.
Could you stand up through four minutes of that?
first_comment: Bonus: most of the deaths came from the tsunamis, not the shaking. Would you know where to run?
